Definition: a primary word; "good" (in any sense, often as noun):--benefit, good(-s, things), well. Compare G2570.
BiblicalUsage: Agathos is 'good' — the commonest word for goodness in the New Testament, used hundreds of times. An evil father still knows how to give good gifts; a good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart; the law is holy, just, and good; and Paul tells us to do good unto all men as we have opportunity. The word covers good things, good people, and the good God behind them all.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe agathos matters because it keeps goodness anchored in God. Good gifts come from the Father, and the good heart is the one the Spirit has remade — goodness is not something I manufacture, it is something God grows.
RelatedTopics: Goodness; Fruit of the Spirit; Character
